title: Carried by Silence, Explained
subtitle: Ylva Onyekwere on how a group chat settles its plans by not replying, and why what turns up on the day is what somebody put their name to
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Ylva Onyekwere's doctoral thesis about the group chats that plan barbecues, birthday parties and working bees. It follows one barbecue's chat from a proposal with two thumbs under it to a park at two o'clock, and sets the census of 318 donated chats beside the 46 occasions she attended with the plan printed as a checklist. The School's Lapse Standard closes it, and Onyekwere describes the census and her argument herself.
topic: A research explainer of the doctoral thesis on how the group chats that plan shared occasions decide, from a census of every proposal in 318 donated chats and 46 occasions attended with the plan printed as a checklist, finding that 88.1 per cent of what became the plan was carried by lapse on a median of two thumbs whether the chat had five members or twenty, and that an item claimed by its bringer arrived 93.3 per cent of the time against 31.2 for an item with no name on it, and closing on the School's Lapse Standard for its committees
